# Aspicio

> Aspicio (Latin: "I look at") is an open-source, TypeScript-first
> drawing engine for DXF and vector PDF: one framework-free
> parse → tessellate pipeline that serves
> people (an interactive WebGL viewer), applications (React components
> and a headless renderer), and AI agents (structured facts, PNG
> renders, and an interactive in-chat viewer over HTTP and MCP).

Aspicio is developed and maintained by [FrontSail AI](https://frontsail.ai/),
released under the MIT license.

## Why Aspicio

- One engine, every surface: the browser viewer, the web components
  and their React/Vue/Svelte bindings, the headless renderer, HTTP
  API, and MCP server are thin adapters over
  the same parse → tessellate core, so a drawing reads identically
  everywhere — no drift between what a person sees and what an agent
  is told.
- Built for AI agents, not retrofitted: `describe_dxf`, `describe_pdf`,
  and `describe_doc` return structured JSON facts (the format read,
  units, bounds, layers with the colors actually drawn, entity counts,
  and the drawing's text content), so an agent reads a title block or a
  dimension value directly — no OCR, no vision round-trip. Their
  `render_*` counterparts return PNGs. The structured tools declare MCP
  output schemas, so clients validate and parse results mechanically
  instead of guessing at shapes.
- An interactive in-chat viewer via the open MCP Apps extension:
  `view_dxf` puts a pannable, zoomable, layer-toggling WebGL viewer
  directly in ChatGPT or Claude conversations, for either format. The widget is locked to
  the drawing the tool call delivered and makes no network requests.
- Broad entity coverage that never fails hard: lines, arcs, circles,
  ellipses, polylines with bulges, splines, TEXT/MTEXT, DIMENSION,
  SOLID/HATCH fills, nested INSERT blocks — anything unsupported is
  counted and reported, never fatal.
- PDF is read as vector line work and text — the paths, strokes, fills,
  and glyphs a PDF/X-4 artwork or dieline carries. Images, shadings, and
  transparency are counted as skipped rather than drawn, so a render
  shows line work rather than a page facsimile, and a scanned PDF
  reports nearly nothing (accurately). Pages become spaces; content
  arrives on a single "Content" layer; measurements are in points,
  because a PDF carries no drawing scale.
- Runs anywhere TypeScript runs: browser, Node, and serverless
  runtimes. WebGL rendering is batched to one draw call per layer, so
  large drawings stay interactive.
- Privacy-first hosted services: no accounts, no stored drawings, and
  guarded URL fetches (private-network blocking, size caps, redirect
  validation, timeouts). Everything is open source.

## Use it

- [Live demo](https://aspicio.frontsail.app/): drop in a DXF or a
  vector PDF and explore it — layer panel, measuring, picking, export.
- [Hosted MCP server](https://aspicio-api.frontsail.app/mcp):
  remote MCP over Streamable HTTP — three describe/render pairs
  (`describe_dxf`/`render_dxf` for DXF, `describe_pdf`/`render_pdf` for
  PDF, `describe_doc`/`render_doc` detecting the format from the bytes)
  plus the `view_dxf` in-chat viewer. No install. A PDF must be given as
  a URL: the inline source form is text, which binary PDF bytes do not
  survive.
- Local MCP server: `npx -y @aspicio/mcp` — adds local-file support,
  reads drawings in-process, never uploads them.
- [HTTP API](https://aspicio-api.frontsail.app/openapi.json):
  `GET /describe?src=<url>` and `GET /render?src=<url>&format=png|svg`
  for DXF, the same two as `/describe-pdf` and `/render-pdf` for PDF,
  and `/describe-doc` and `/render-doc` for either — self-described via
  OpenAPI 3.1.
- npm packages: `@aspicio/core` (viewer + headless pipeline),
  `@aspicio/elements` (framework-neutral web components:
  `<aspicio-embed>`, `<aspicio-preview>`, `<aspicio-layer-panel>`),
  and `@aspicio/react` / `@aspicio/vue` / `@aspicio/svelte` (the same
  three components — `<AspicioEmbed>`, `<AspicioPreview>`, `<AspicioLayerPanel>` —
  as thin framework bindings over the elements).
